What does it mean to be kingdom people? What is the nature of this kingdom? What is our responsibility to the world we find ourselves a part of? If Jesus is coming to bring His kingdom and to rule over the earth, can’t we just sit and wait for that to happen? As we consider this model prayer, especially the petition “ Your kingdom come. Your will be done…, ” we will seek to discover our responsibility as local representatives of the kingdom of God.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Kings 6
description: Elisha revealed God's protection over Israel through the miracles he performed. When enemy armies surrounded him, God opened his servant’s eyes to see heavenly forces at work. In this message, Pastor Skip Heitzig shares how God’s power is greater than our fear and encourages us to trust Him in every situation.
speaker: Skip

title: How to Build a Kingdom City
description: As believers living in an ungodly world, it's easy to wonder if we can actually make a difference. It can be tempting to complain when we see the darkness and division around us, but God calls us to be His hands—to do the work because our city is worth saving. In this message, Nate Heitzig looks to the life of Nehemiah as we discover how to act as agents of change in our city.      Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: guest:Nate Heitzig

title: 2 Kings 4:22-5:27
description: In 2 Kings 4-5, Elisha performed miracles, reviving a widow’s son and healing Naaman of leprosy. While Naaman—a Syrian—obeyed and was cleansed, Elisha’s servant Gehazi’s disobedience and lack of faith resulted in judgment. In this message, Skip Heitzig shares how faith and obedience invite God’s blessings.
speaker: Skip

title: Heaven’s Capital City
description:
Today we will conduct a  walk-through  of every believer’s ultimate destination—the capital city of the eternal state, called  New Jerusalem . Unlike New York, New Jersey, New Hampshire, or New Mexico, this future place will have the most unique environment ever. I will touch on seven highlights of this future cityscape that make heaven the world’s most interesting destination.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Kings 3:1-4:26
description: It can be easy to get overwhelmed by circumstances that seem too difficult to face, but as believers, we should approach a situation in light of God's ability to bring us through it. In this message, Skip Heitzig looks at miracles God performed when hope seemed lost as He faithfully provided for the needs of His people.
speaker: Skip

title: Shocking Truths About Heaven
description:
Our ideas about what heaven will be like may not necessarily be how Scripture describes our eternal home. After officiating hundreds of funerals, I’ve heard some pretty bizarre remarks about loved ones turning into angels or greeting St. Peter at heaven’s gates or engaging in their favorite hobbies. As we look at the final phase of heaven, what is called  the eternal state , we read things that may be shocking to some, including that it will come complete with a capital city.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Kings 1-2
description: God's faithfulness will always prevail—His leadership preserves His will and prophecies. In this first message from the book of 2 Kings, Skip Heitzig compares the failings of human leadership with God's perfect, faithful leadership.
speaker: Skip

title: The Last Judgment
description:
Contemplate the phrase  the wrath of God . Most people who hear it think of God as some sort of annoyed deity—one who has a short temper and lashes out in uncontrolled rage. Actually, God’s wrath, including His judgment of unbelievers, is part of His moral integrity. God cannot just withhold judgment; that would go against His moral integrity. The final judgment of God will be His great complement to human freedom and choice. For those who choose to live without God, they will!   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 21-22
description: In 1 Kings 21-22, we see the cost of pride and corruption through Ahab and Jezebel’s story, but we also glimpse God’s justice and mercy at work. Even when earthly leaders fail, God’s purposes prevail. Join Skip Heitzig as he reminds us to walk humbly, seek God's truth, and trust His sovereignty in every situation.
speaker: Skip

title: What Happens When You Die?
description:
As a society, our attention is often captured by the idea of the afterlife. Many books and movies have been dedicated to the question of what happens next. But the answers can be found in the Word, not the world. In this message from Luke 16, Nate Heitzig explores a glimpse of what comes next and asks, "Do you choose Jesus today?"  
    

    Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: guest:Nate Heitzig

title: The Perfect Government
description:
The phrase  perfect government  sounds like an oxymoron. Our world has never known such perfection, and Utopia seems to be the stuff of fairytales. But the Bible promises a coming kingdom on earth, ruled by the Messiah, Jesus Christ. These predictions are widely scattered through the Old Testament and reaffirmed in the New. But only in Revelation 20 are we given the duration of one thousand years. Today I want to share four marks of the governmental structure during the millennium. 
   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 20
description: In 1 Kings 20, God showed His power through an unexpected victory for the Israelites, showing that no enemy is too strong when God fights for His people. Pastor Skip reminds us that even when the odds seem stacked against us, we can trust God’s plan.
speaker: Skip

title: A Thousand Years of Peace
description:
Can you envision, or even imagine, a world without conflict or war—a peace-filled, fair, and just environment? This has been the stuff of dreams, fairytales, and fiction. Bumper stickers tell us to “Visualize World Peace,” yet we find it impossible to do so because of our own history. But it is actually scheduled to happen for an entire millennium! For the next two weeks, we will explore this theme of the kingdom age—an era dominated by righteousness, justice, and goodness.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 19
description: In 1 Kings 19, Elijah found himself at rock bottom, feeling alone and defeated, but God met him there—not in a grand display of power, but in a gentle whisper. In this message, Skip Heitzig reminds us that God’s strength often comes in quiet moments. When life overwhelms, listen closely: God is still speaking, guiding, and renewing your purpose.
speaker: Skip

title: The Second Coming: Part 2
description:
The second coming will be the most important event in the world accomplished by the most important person in the world. It has no parallel. The second coming of Christ will be utterly unlike His first coming. The first time He came born in obscurity—unnoticed and unhonored. He shall come the second time in splendor and be seen by all. Billy Graham once said, “The second coming of Christ will be so revolutionary that it will change every aspect of life on this planet.” It will effectively end history as we know it and ready the world for a glorious kingdom age.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 17:17-18:46
description: God clearly demonstrated His power through Elijah—first by raising a widow’s son, then by confronting the prophets of Baal in a dramatic showdown on Mount Carmel. Fire fell, hearts repented, and rain finally returned to the land. In this message, Skip Heitzig explains that God alone answers with power, and bold faith often leads to bold results.
speaker: Skip

title: Sunday 11 am - Discussion Panel with Skip Heitzig, Dr. Frank Turek & Alisa Childers
description:
Dr. Frank Turek is a dynamic speaker, TV show host, podcaster, and award-winning author. As president of crossexamined.org, he presents powerful and entertaining evidence for Christianity. He is a widely featured apologetics expert and cultural commentator and has appeared on hundreds of radio programs and top TV networks including Fox News, ABC, and CBS. 
   
 Alisa Childers is a lifelong churchgoer, follower of Jesus, former CCM recording artist with the Dove Award-winning band ZOEgirl, as well as an apologist and author.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 16:31-17:16
description: As Ahab led Israel into unprecedented idolatry, God raised up Elijah to confront the nation’s rebellion. In the midst of drought and judgment, God miraculously provided for Elijah and a widow in desperate need. Join Pastor Skip Heitzig as he explores how God’s provision is never limited by our circumstances and how He often uses unlikely people in unlikely places to carry out His plan.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 15:17-16:34
description: In these verses, we see how Israel's kings descended deeper into corruption and wickedness, with each new leader outdoing the last. From Baasha to Ahab, power was misused, God was ignored, and sin became normalized. Follow along as Pastor Skip examines broken governance—highlighting that when leadership abandons truth, decay spreads quickly—and God never overlooks it.
speaker: Skip

title: The Second Coming
description:
The second coming of Jesus Christ is the moment we have all been waiting for—from the very beginning of human history until now. It is the capstone of God’s redemptive plan, and it is the only hope for the future. After history runs its course of rebellion, after Satan’s age-old retaliation, after God’s closing judgments on the earth, the end of the world as we know it will come. There are eight noticeable features of Christ’s second coming. Today we will cover the first four.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 14:1-15:24
description: Israel and Judah spiraled deeper into spiritual decline as one king after another turned from the Lord. Even brief moments of reform were overshadowed by patterns of compromise. Skip Heitzig digs into these verses to reveal how godly leadership matters.
speaker: Skip

title: The Battle of Armageddon
description:
The very word  Armageddon  sends shivers through the soul! Most everyone has heard the term (or seen the movie). The word even gets mentioned from time to time by world leaders. Most everyone understands it to be a reference to some final battle. But today let’s drill down deeper than just a fictional Hollywood film about an asteroid destroyed by a warhead. Today we will examine five facets of this culminating military campaign, including what will bring it to an end.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 12:25-13:34
description: Jeroboam created a counterfeit religion of fear, leading Israel away from true worship. God sent a prophet to confront him, but even he disobeyed. In this message, Skip Heitzig emphasizes that compromise—no matter the motive—leads to spiritual drift, and partial obedience is still disobedience.
speaker: Skip

title: Six Six Six
description: The infamous number  666  has been the cause of fear and superstition for generations. If people spot it on a license plate or a grocery store receipt, they consider it a bad omen. It’s right up there with the number  13 . Many good expositors differ widely when it comes to interpreting its meaning. Will it be an implanted chip? An ID card? A barcode tattooed into the skin or simply a mark identifying allegiance to Antichrist’s kingdom? Today we will consider three additional details of Antichrist’s coming influence and try to drill down on the meaning of the  mark of the beast .
speaker: Skip

title: Freedom Celebration 2023
description: Each of us has an empty space in our soul waiting to be filled. But the tendency to fill that hole with people, possessions, or experiences only leaves us dissatisfied and reaching for more. As believers, we choose to acknowledge our dependence upon our Savior and that is the source of our freedom. In this message, Skip Heitzig encourages us to take our doubts and questions to the God who made us.
speaker: Skip

title: The Antichrist Revealed
description:
The subject of the  Antichrist  is one of the most speculated, debated, and ridiculed subjects in all of Scripture. Who he will be, where he’ll be from, and what he will do is the theme of countless books, movies, and dissertations, as well as jokes and memes. But this is a serious subject. There are over 100 passages in the Bible that describe this person. Revelation 13 is one of the more famous. Let’s consider six characteristics of this leader who will live up to his terrible name.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 11:14-12:24
description: As Solomon’s heart turned from God, the consequences rippled outward, and cracks began to form throughout Israel. After Solomon’s death, his son Rehoboam rejected wise counsel and embraced pride, sparking a national split that divided Israel and Judah. In this message, Pastor Skip examines how unchecked compromise and stubborn leadership can fracture what God has built. The decisions we make today can shape generations to come—for better or worse.
speaker: Skip

title: Home for My Heart - Vision Weekend
description: Everyone has a next step toward taking ownership of their family, church, and city. None of us can do everything, but everyone can do something. And if everyone does something, we believe we’re going to find that anything is possible. Write down your next step in each of the three areas of focus for our 2023 vision so you can join us in saying, “This place. These people. My privilege.”
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 10:1-11:13
description: In 1 Kings 10, we see that Solomon’s wisdom and wealth had impressed the Queen of Sheba and the watching world. But the picture quickly shifted—Solomon’s heart drifted from the Lord as he accumulated foreign wives and compromised his devotion. What began with wisdom ended in divided loyalty. In this message, Pastor Skip Heitzig warns how spiritual decline often begins with small compromises, and he urges believers to guard our hearts and remain fully committed to the God who gives every good gift.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 8:54-9:28
description: After dedicating the temple, Solomon blessed the people and reminded them of God’s faithfulness. In response, the Lord appeared to him again, affirming His covenant, but also warned that obedience is the key to lasting blessing. As Solomon’s influence grew, the seeds of distraction began to show. Pastor Skip reminds us that while success is a gift from God, it must be anchored in faithfulness—or it can quickly become a substitute for dependence on Him.
speaker: Skip

title: How Bad Can It Get?
description:
Just how bad will the coming  day of the Lord  be for the people of planet Earth? Is the tribulation period simply a scare tactic of doomsday fanatics who love to sensationalize everything? Today we consider an overview of this time period in the book of Revelation. We’ll see both the lowlights and the highlights of this coming seven-year time frame. Hint: some things might surprise you!   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 8:1-54
description: Solomon brought the ark of the covenant into the temple, and the glory of the Lord descended. As Solomon prayed before the people, he acknowledged God’s faithfulness, pleaded for His mercy, and dedicated the temple as a place where heaven touches earth. Skip Heitzig emphasizes that while the temple was magnificent, it was also a reminder of God's desire to dwell with His people. This passage calls us to be people of prayer, humility, and wholehearted devotion—because God always meets His people when they seek Him.
speaker: Skip

title: The Flow of the Future
description:
I admit that the book of Revelation can appear mysterious, full of curious symbols and imagery. But it’s actually more straightforward than you may think. If you hold to a grammatical/historical view, this book provides a chronological flow of future history. It presents Jesus evaluating His church, judging His world, proclaiming His gospel, saving His nation, and establishing His kingdom. For this week and next, we will consider  the flow of the future. 
     
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 7
description: Through 1 Kings 7, we're reminded to build lives that reflect God’s glory, not our own. While the temple came first in priority, Solomon’s palace took nearly twice as long to complete, which reflected both his devotion and humanity. Skip Heitzig highlights how beauty, craftsmanship, and order reflect the character of God—and warns against letting when comfort overshadow our calling.
speaker: Skip

title: How Moms Can Change the World
description:
Today we pay a special tribute to those unique individuals we call mothers. They have given us life on this earth, and their influence has transformed our lives. Here in this passage, Paul the apostle pays special tribute to two women who changed the world by seeing their duty as a divine mission. They raised a future leader who helped shape the early years of Christianity through tenderness, godliness, and boldness. These attributes are vital for all of us to have.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 5-6
description: With peace in the land and wisdom from above, Solomon began the monumental task of building the temple. Every detail, every stone, and every beam pointed to God’s holiness and faithfulness to His promises. In 1 Kings 5-6, Pastor Skip Heitzig dives further into how God uses seasons of peace to build something lasting—and how our lives, like the temple, are meant to be a dwelling place for His presence.
speaker: Skip

title: The Rapture: What & When
description:
The subject of the end times is  fascinating  and should also be  motivating . One thing it should not be is  aggravating ; it shouldn’t produce fear but rather hope. Some of the young believers in the church at Thessalonica were perturbed and afraid thinking they were facing the tribulation and that loved ones who had died had missed the rapture Paul told them about. Paul’s concern wasn’t just doctrinal but pastoral—he wanted to comfort the Thessalonians. Let’s dig deeper into this doctrine.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 3:9-4:34
description: Solomon asked for wisdom—and God answered in a big way. Not only did he receive discernment to lead God’s people, but his wisdom became legendary, drawing attention from nations near and far. In this message, Pastor Skip Heitzig examines how God honors a heart that seeks Him first, and how spiritual wisdom isn’t just about knowing truth—it’s about living it out every day.
speaker: Skip

title: The Rapture of the Church
description:
The phrase  rapture of the church  was a foreign one to me. I never heard it growing up and didn’t believe it was real  until  I read the Bible. Not only do I now believe in the rapture of the church, I believe it could happen at any moment! This passage of Scripture is what E. Schuyler English called “the first New Testament intimation of the Rapture.” Today we will be encouraged by Jesus’ own promise of it. Next week we’ll look more deeply at the timing of it.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 2:1-3:10
description: David passed the mantle of leadership to Solomon with a charge to walk faithfully with God. Solomon stepped into the throne room—and into a world of political tension, personal responsibility, and divine opportunity. In this teaching, we see what it means to lead with a heart aligned with God, and how true strength begins with surrender and seeking Him first.
speaker: Skip

title: Defeat of the Russian Alliance
description:
These two chapters describe an event that will occur after Israel is restored to its land but before the millennial kingdom is established. There are so many remarkable aspects to this future battle. The list of nations (which today are forming alliances) is one. Another is how they will be overthrown. Other nations will watch but will not come to Israel’s aid. Only God will intervene. Let’s get some further details of this future invasion and how God will use it to bring glory to Himself.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Kings 1
description: As King David's life came to an end, a power struggle erupted over who would sit on the throne next. While one son seized control, another waited for God’s timing—and in the chaos, we see the tension between human ambition and divine appointment. In this message, Pastor Skip Heitzig explains what it means to trust God’s plan over our own and reminds us that His plans always prevail.
speaker: Skip

title: The Coming Invasion of Russia
description:
I realize that my sermon title today seems like it could have been a headline from a Ukrainian newspaper in early February 2022. But it actually will be a headline in the  Jerusalem Post  at some future date. The role of Russia in biblical prophecy, along with a group of nations in strategic alliance with its leader, is noteworthy. Who will they attack? When will it happen? And what is their motivation for this major military incursion of such a tiny country like Israel? Let’s find out.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: The Heist: How Jesus Robbed the Grave!
description: Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Why Israel Must Survive
description:
The land of Israel has been described as “the most important piece of real estate on earth,” “the geographical platform on which the story of the Bible is staged,” “the center of divine dealing with nations,” “the spiritual navel of the world,” and “ground zero for the end times.” Jerusalem has been called “the only city on earth not up for negotiations with anyone at any time for any reason.” Over and over again, God promised Israel “a future and a hope” (Jeremiah 29:11). Let’s again consider how and why Israel stands at center stage for the fulfillment of end-time prophecy.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: The Role of Israel in Prophecy
description:
One of the great questions that has persisted throughout church history has to do with the future of the nation of Israel. Is God finished with Israel as a nation? Will there be a literal regathering and spiritual restoration? Or is all that figurative and allegorical, meaning that the promises to Israel are now subsumed by the church? Today and for the next few weeks we will consider these questions. We begin with the  Abrahamic covenant —God’s unconditional promises made to the nation’s founder.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Daniel’s 70th Week
description:
Last week, we considered how God tells time as we explored the detailed timetable of Israel’s future, including the prediction of the Messiah’s coming and death. Today we will consider the final period of that time clock, the seventieth week. We typically refer to it as the tribulation, a period that is given the greatest explanation in Revelation 6-19. God achieved redemption for the world by the end of the sixty-ninth week through the death of the Messiah, but the overall goal will require the seventieth.   
 
    Watch this Week's Connect Group Video  
     
    70 Weeks of Daniel - Timeline Chart
speaker: Skip

title: How God Tells Time—Daniel’s 70 Weeks
description:
God inhabits eternity but reveals Himself throughout time. Moreover, He wants us to understand what He is up to and what His plans are for the future. Amos declared, “Surely the Lord  God  does nothing, unless He reveals His secret to His servants the prophets” (Amos 3:7). God gave to Daniel the prophet the most remarkable timetable for Israel’s future that would lead up to the coming of the Messiah, the tribulation period, and even the kingdom age. Daniel 9 has been called  the Backbone of Prophecy . For the next two weeks, we will seek to unravel and understand it.   
 
    Watch this Week's Connect Group Video  
     
    70 Weeks of Daniel - Timeline Chart
speaker: Skip

title: Rapture Ready
description: Paul encouraged believers not to grieve without hope, reminding them that those who have died in Christ will be raised when He returns. Pastor Nate Heitzig dives into 1 Thessalonians to provide deeper insight into death—the great separator, and Jesus—the great reconciler, who has removed the hold that death and sin have on our lives.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: guest:Nate Heitzig

title: The Millennium: The Great Theological Divide
description:
The Old and New Testaments include numerous references to the kingdom of the Messiah. It is one of the most frequently mentioned subjects in the Bible. Jesus Himself even taught us to pray, “Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven” (Matthew 6:10, KJV). But this subject has become a point of division throughout church history. Three major viewpoints have emerged. Today we examine them and consider the millennium’s chronology, theology, and necessity.   
  Watch this Week's Connect Group Video  
   

  Chronology of the End Times
speaker: Skip

title: The Problem of Christ’s Return
description: How could the return of Jesus Christ ever be a problem? It certainly won’t be a problem for anyone who trusts in Him. The problem lies in understanding its timing and manner. When and how will Jesus return? How can we say that Jesus can come back at any time and that we should always be ready for Him knowing He said certain signs must happen  first ? How do we reconcile all the prophetic signs the Bible predicts must happen (including the great tribulation and worldwide devastation) and yet say Jesus is coming soon? Hint: you already know the answer!     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: The End Is Near?
description: Welcome to a study of  eschatology , or end times. In the next several weeks, we will be looking into one of the most discussed topics in all of Scripture—the last days and the end of the world. While this is not necessarily a lightweight or feel-good subject matter, it will actually make you feel good  if  you’re on the right side of it! Four words can be used to sum up the experience of this theme of the last days. These four words will form the basis of our studies in coming weeks.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: What Every Church Should Do
description: It seems that everyone is an armchair theologian these days, expressing their opinion of what churches should (and shouldn’t) do! From declaring that churches should stay away from contemporary, especially political, topics to saying the church should just be concerned about social issues. But as Paul closed out his letter to the church at Colosse, he informed them—and us—of what churches should be focused on. These final verses give five directives for any church.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: With a Little Help from My Friends
description: I admit I stole the sermon title from the 1967 Beatles song of this same name. That aside, the truth is  we were never designed to do life alone!  Isolation is the death knell of a productive and satisfying life. Someone once said that a friend is “one who walks in when the rest of the world walks out.” In this brief pericope, we gain understanding as to how Christian friendships should work.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Marks of Healthy Relationships
description: God’s leaders have always leaned on others to support them in their work. Paul was no different. He didn’t operate a one-man show. Rather, he was a team builder who spread the load of ministry among others, many of whom were suspect and questionable. But Paul himself was once suspect and questionable. In these closing remarks, we get insight into what attributes make for strong, healthy, and effective relationships. Today let’s consider two guys who displayed four qualities.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Corinthians 1:1-11
description: Believers in Corinth faced spiritual tension on two fronts—they were caught between a pagan culture and false teachers trying to usurp the apostles' authority. In this message, Skip Heitzig lays out the situation in Corinth, examines Paul's authority-establishing greeting to the church, and begins to unpack the apostle's theology of suffering and consolation.
speaker: Skip

title: Prophecy Update
description: Four out of ten Americans believe we are living in the end times, a topic often misunderstood, sensationalized, or ignored altogether. Next to the topic of faith itself, the theme of the second coming dominates the Scriptures, and as believers, there are aspects of our future we can be certain of—the prophecies of Scripture will be fulfilled. In this message, Skip Heitzig encourages us to prepare our hearts for Jesus’ return as we see “the beginning of sorrows” (Matthew 24:8) in the world around us.   Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Into the Light
description: Christianity isn’t creed—it’s a connection. John had seen, heard, and touched Jesus, and in his first epistle, he invites modern day believers into that same real, joyful fellowship with God. But that relationship requires honesty: Walking in the light, confessing our sins, and trusting that God is faithful to cleanse and restore us completely.
speaker: Skip

title: Into the Night a Light Shines
description: John started his gospel by taking us back to the very beginning—before time, before creation—revealing Jesus as the eternal Word. He is not just from God; He is God. Through Him, everything was made, and in Him, we receive life and light. In this message, Pastor Skip Heitzig reminds us that even in a dark world, His light keeps shining—undiminished, undefeated, and unstoppable.
speaker: Skip

title: Into the Night: Wise Men’s Delight
description: Joseph and Mary were pushed  into the night  by the innkeeper, local shepherds went  into the night  to find the Infant who was announced by angels, and now the Magi were traveling westward  into the night  following a star. Who were these mysterious men and why had they come? How did they know to show up in Jerusalem and then Bethlehem? What prompted them to bow and worship this Child? Today we probe the familiar story to learn from their background and journey to Christ the King.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 24
description: Even our failures can become moments of worship when we return to God with repentance and trust in His restoring grace. In 2 Samuel 24, David’s pride led to a costly census, but God turned judgment into mercy. His story ended with sacrifice, a renewed altar, and redemption.
speaker: Skip

title: Into the Night: A Shepherd's Surprise
description: Experts tell us that breaking up your routine can be healthy and can help you to eliminate burnout. Predictability and monotonous activity can stifle creativity and even lead to depression. For a group of shepherds whose work was uneventful and often boring, everything was about to change from a nighttime encounter that shattered their routine and gave them a new sense of purpose. Their story is one of the best parts of the Christmas narrative. Let’s take a fresh look at their experience.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Into the Night: A Couple’s First Christmas
description:
Robert Browning quipped, “Night conceals a world but reveals a
universe.” Kids are often afraid of the dark, preferring a brightly
lit room to the pitch black of night. But the Christmas story is
shrouded in the darkness of the nighttime sky. Its events took place
in a barely lit stable after the innkeeper had pushed Joseph and his
very pregnant wife away from shelter and into the night. But God’s
universal plan would be revealed through this humble birth. Today we
begin this short series by looking at Christmas through the experience
of this couple from Nazareth.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 23
description: God doesn’t require perfection—simply faithfulness, courage, and reliance on His strength. In 2 Samuel 23, David reflected on his legacy. And though he was flawed, he is still remembered as a man who chased hard after God’s heart.
speaker: Skip

title: Speak Up!
description: Communication is a basic human trait, and one of the most obvious differences between people and animals is our ability to form articulate speech. We can inform, persuade, instruct, motivate, and encourage. The Christian, in particular, is called upon to speak to God about people and speak to people about God. The “new man” (Colossians 3:10) has a new mouth and a new message. Let’s consider four ways that we as believers can communicate to God and others.
speaker: Skip

title: Weekend of Generosity
description: The biggest question in life is not what you own, but what owns  you . As believers, our generosity is a gauge of our faith, and how we manage our finances is a gauge of our spiritual growth, because we are never more like Jesus than when we give. In this message, Skip Heitzig reminds us that it’s not about how much God has trusted us with, but rather, it’s about how we use what we have to further His kingdom.   Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 21-22
description: David confronted unresolved national sin and avenged past wrongs, then turned to praise, creating a powerful declaration of God’s faithfulness. It reminds us that even after failure and struggle, we can still choose gratitude—because God’s grace will outlast every storm.
speaker: Skip

title: How the Gospel Transforms the Workplace
description: Our faith in Jesus Christ not only changes  us , but it also changes  families  and it changes  communities . Or at least it should! Every corner of our culture should feel the “salt and light” that is created from the transformed Christian lives within it. Just as Paul had instructed wives, husbands, children, and parents within the home, he now instructs the servants and masters who make up the social world. We can glean much about what our actions and attitudes in the workplace should be like.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 19:40-20:26
description: When David returned to Jerusalem, tribal tensions rose, and another rebellion began to brew. Joab violently secured order, but the peace he won was fragile and temporary. Disunity often follows unrest—and without spiritual restoration, people remain divided even after the dust settles.
speaker: Skip

title: The Four-Legged Stool of a Godly Home
description: A four-legged stool can meet the contours of an uneven floor much better than a three-legged one, and it can handle the displacement of weight more efficiently. Life is much the same way. A bumpy world requires the stability provided by a family. If each family member is aligned with God’s will, the weight of life’s trials will be much easier to bear. The strength and solidity of a good and godly home is society’s greatest asset. Let’s consider four basic roles for a successful family unit.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Guardrails to Knowing God’s Will
description: Today I am grateful to Mr. Dean Sicking, an American inventor who invented the first energy-absorbing guardrail for US roadways to keep our cars on the highway. But did you know there are also guardrails to keep our lives in the lane of God’s will? After describing the  character  of the new man (the saved and transformed person), Paul turns to our  conduct . He gives to us four guardrails that will keep our lives “between the white lines” of the will of God.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 18:1-19:39
description: In 2 Samuel 18 and 19, we see David’s victory over Absalom, but that victory was overshadowed by deep personal grief. Though justice had been served, a father mourned the loss of his son. Obedience to God sometimes brings personal pain, but grief must yield to purpose.
speaker: Skip

title: A New Set of Clothes for a New Way of Life
description: The global fashion market is a $1.55 trillion industry. It’s because everyone wears clothes! From birth to death, people cover themselves with apparel both for warmth and for style. The Christian believer should also have a spiritual closet filled with the right (and righteous) garments. Paul has been speaking about the “old man” versus the “new man,” and he does so using a fashion metaphor. In these three verses, he explains how every Christian can  dress for success !     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 16-17
description: God’s providence is always at work—even through seasons of pain and opposition. David faced betrayal, slander, and physical danger as Absalom’s rebellion intensified. While some cursed and others plotted, God quietly worked behind the scenes to protect David and frustrate the plans of the wicked. When we trust God in the dark, He will make a way forward in the light.
speaker: Skip

title: Pastor Skip & Paul Clark Celebrate Decades of Ministry
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 14:23-15:37
description: When appearances replace repentance, the consequences can be devastating. In 2 Samuel 14-15, we see Absalom's return to Jerusalem, but reconciliation with David remained surface-level. Bitterness festered, and Absalom began to steal the hearts of the people, eventually launching a rebellion against his father. Conflict left unresolved breeds division, but true restoration begins in the heart and must be rooted in humility and truth.
speaker: Skip

title: Living on Earth While Aiming at Heaven
description: Today’s message title may sound suspiciously similar to last week’s message title. That’s because we are dealing with two different sides of the same coin. Paul began this chapter by focusing our attention on heaven in the first four verses. Now he brings us back down to earth where we are slugging it out in the trenches of sensuality and hatred. While on our way to heaven, we are still doing battle on earth. Paul tells us that heavenly citizens should take three firm steps while living on earth.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 13:1-14:25
description: Unchecked sin doesn’t just damage individuals, it can fracture families and erode leadership. David’s family was torn apart by sin, silence, and sorrow. Amnon’s evil act against Tamar set off a chain of bitterness, vengeance, and unresolved conflict. This passage is a sobering reminder that ignoring sin will only multiply its consequences, but God still calls us to truth, justice, and restoration.
speaker: Skip

title: Aiming at Heaven While Living on Earth
description: “Earth has no sorrow that heaven cannot heal,” said Thomas Moore. But if that is true, why don’t we think more about heaven? Why do we only think and talk about heaven at funerals? How can the reality of our future home motivate our activities right now? If you were to think about your life in terms of chronology, how much time do you have left on earth? Let’s look at three categories of truth that will help us aim at heaven while we are living on earth.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 11-12
description: Brokenness can become the doorway to restoration—if we choose to come clean before the Lord. In 2 Samuel 11–12, David’s failure with Bathsheba led to a devastating chain of sin, cover-up, and consequence. But when he was confronted by the prophet Nathan, David chose to respond with repentance. No one is above falling, but no one is beyond God’s grace.
speaker: Skip

title: When Religion Gets Wacky
description: Karl Marx insisted that “religion is the opium of the people,” while Napoleon Bonaparte suggested that “religion is what keeps the poor from murdering the rich.” But within the broad category of religious belief are ideologies and practices that are dangerous and silly because they distract people from the essence of truth. God made it simple by having His Son do for us what we could never do on our own—reach God! Religion takes what is simple and merely complicates it.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 9-10
description: In these verses, David showed unexpected kindness—first to Mephibosheth, the disabled son of Jonathan, and then to the Ammonite king. His actions reflected the heart of God: Grace extended to the undeserving. Real strength is often shown through compassion, and that mercy, not might, can make the deepest impact.
speaker: Skip

title: Jesus Paid It All!
description: Sitting in the choir loft one Sunday morning, Elvina Hall, inspired by a sermon, wrote in the flyleaf of her songbook the words to a now-famous hymn: “Jesus paid it all; all to Him I owe.” Paul expressed much the same thing in this paragraph. After telling his readers they were complete in Christ, he then showed them how that was so. Against the backdrop of false teachers, some of whom insisted on performing rituals, Paul showed exactly what Jesus had done.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 7-8
description: David wanted to build a house for God—but God flipped the script and promised to build David a lasting dynasty instead. It was a moment of divine grace and covenant which serves as a powerful reminder that God’s plans are always greater than our own. When we prioritize God’s glory, He often surprises us with blessings we didn’t expect.
speaker: Skip

title: What Keeps an Apostle Up at Night?
description: Jesus Christ is the most controversial person who has ever lived! There are as many opinions about Him as there are religions, cults, philosophies, and church denominations. Though Paul had never met the young Christians in the church of Colosse, he was deeply concerned for them since attractive, man-made philosophies were making inroads. He wanted them to know the truth, to grow in their faith, and to be careful of any human ideas that diminish the place of Jesus Christ. I have summed up Paul’s concerns with three simple directives:  Believe! Behave! Beware!        Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 6
description: In 2 Samuel 6, David brought the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem—but not without costly missteps. God's holiness should never be taken lightly. Our good intentions must align with God’s instructions. Skip Heitzig highlights how true worship is both joyful and reverent—God desires our celebration, but He also requires our obedience.
speaker: Skip

title: Serving Christ in an Unchristian World
description: Serving Christ is the result of being saved by Christ. But the Christian life should carry a warning label: “Warning: Those who enter here won’t find it easy. In fact, at times it will be very difficult, but it will be the greatest adventure ever!” In this paragraph, Paul opened the curtain on his own personal life as a servant of Christ and shared five characteristics of his own ministry. Are they yours?     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 4-5
description: In 2 Samuel 2:12–3:39, we see the struggle for God’s kingdom as it unfolded through conflict and fragile alliances. Even amid political turmoil and personal rivalry, God’s hand was at work preparing the way for His chosen king. Pastor Skip Heitzig examines why it's important to trust God’s timing, even when the path seems uncertain.
speaker: Skip

title: Reconciled!
description: Today we come to one of the most important truths of the New Testament—that we have been reconciled to God. The gap that separates humans from their Creator has been closed by one person and one action. The results of that act are what brings God and His rebel creatures into a restored relationship. Let’s take a deeper dive into these magnificent realities and what they mean to us.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 2:12-3:39
description: In 2 Samuel 2:12–3:39, we see the struggle for God’s kingdom as it unfolded through conflict and fragile alliances. Even amid political turmoil and personal rivalry, God’s hand was at work preparing the way for His chosen king. Pastor Skip Heitzig examines why it's important to trust God’s timing, even when the path seems uncertain.
speaker: Skip

title: Why Jesus Is Supreme
description: A popular college class in most philosophy departments compares the beliefs of major world religions, including Christianity. Jesus is presented as one among many options to believe in. He is typically explained as a poor Jewish itinerant preacher who resisted the religious system and got into trouble because of it. But the Bible doesn’t present Him that way. Scripture presents Jesus as the supreme One—the unmatched, superlative, preeminent progenitor of everything in existence.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 2 Samuel 1:1-2:11
description: In 2 Samuel 1:1–2:11, David grieved deeply over the deaths of Saul and Jonathan, showing us that faith includes honoring God’s timing—even in loss. In this message, Pastor Skip Heitzig reminds us that God often prepares our hearts for His purposes through sorrow.
speaker: Skip

title: How to Pray for Believers
description: Before theology must come  knee -ology! Praying is one of the most basic activities of anyone’s spiritual life. Before Paul got into the nitty-gritty of the great theological heart of this letter (the supremacy of Christ), he prayed for the believers in Colosse. What he prayed for is a good template for us in praying for other Christians. It’s eye-opening to discover the items that are on his list. (Spoiler alert: He didn’t pray for their health, finances, or relationships—though there’s nothing wrong with that.) Paul’s prayer requests were more basic, more to the heart of core issues.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 16
description: Christians are sometimes accused of being so heavenly minded that they're no earthly good. But the question we should be asking is, "How can you be much earthly good unless you are heavenly minded?" As believers, it is impossible to detach the future from the present—our future in heaven should motivate our lives on earth. In this message from 1 Corinthians 16, Skip Heitzig encourages you to be motivated in the present by the truth of the future.
speaker: Skip

title: What Makes Christians So Great?
description: One of the best compliments you could ever receive is, “You are a great Christian.” Of course, there are no perfect people and thus no perfect Christians. But every true Christian is a great Christian because of five traits observed by the apostle Paul in this paragraph of Colossians. He was thankful for the work of Christ in their lives, which rendered them valuable (great) in the sight of God and for the purpose of His cause. Let’s explore them.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 15:20-58
description: As believers, we look forward to the completion of our salvation through resurrection, but God is not only interested in saving your soul—He also wants to redeem your body. Your physical body is like a seed that has been sown. What comes from the seed, though it is related, will be vastly different. In this teaching, Skip Heitzig reminds us that, just like plants or grain or flowers, the sowing is lowly compared to the glory and beauty of what comes from it.
speaker: Skip

title: Always Only Jesus
description: We live in an age when science is not only revered but also followed with religious fervor. We also live in an age of division and deception both within the church and without. Two thousand years ago, the church at Colossae experienced similar cultural and ideological tensions as the Colossian heresy, a mixture of Greek mysticism and Jewish legalism, threatened to destroy the church. In this message, Pastor Skip introduces the book of Colossians, describing the apostle Paul's concern for the church, his correspondence to the church, and the character of the church.     Watch this Week's Connect Group Video
speaker: Skip

title: Freedom Celebration 2022
description: Freedom Celebration July 1, 2022 from Calvary Church
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 15:1-34
description: Raising the dead isn't difficult for the God who created life to begin with. Jesus' resurrection provides the template for the physical resurrection of the saints. The apostle Paul explained the significance of the resurrection to our faith in 1 Corinthians 15—if Christ is not risen, our faith is futile. In this teaching, Skip Heitzig reminds you of the hope you can find in the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
speaker: Skip

title: Church: A Place for Purpose
description: To belong is to be accepted. To belong is to feel secure. Without belonging, we are isolated and alone. Our greatest desire as humans is to know and be known, to love and be loved, and to feel confident that those who know and love us will be there for us through thick and thin. Mother Teresa, the tireless servant in Calcutta’s slums, said, “If we have no peace, it is because we have forgotten that we belong to each other.” That is never truer than in the church. This new society that Jesus calls His  church  is where we find connection to God and a sense of belonging.
speaker: Skip

title: Wrinkles & Ripples
description: Faithfulness can overcome the most difficult circumstances, resulting in a legacy of faith that ripples through multiple generations.
speaker: guest:Kevin Miller

title: 1 Corinthians 14:1-35
description: The best gift of the Spirit is the gift God has for you, and that depends on the situations and circumstances in which you find yourself. That's why living life under the movement and supervision of the Holy Spirit is so important, because we all encounter everyday situations that demand different things at different times. In this teaching, Skip Heitzig highlights the importance of properly exercising our spiritual gifts at the right times.
speaker: Skip

title: Church: A Place for Belonging
description: To belong is to be accepted. To belong is to feel secure. Without belonging, we are isolated and alone. Our greatest desire as humans is to know and be known, to love and be loved, and to feel confident that those who know and love us will be there for us through thick and thin. Mother Teresa, the tireless servant in Calcutta’s slums, said, “If we have no peace, it is because we have forgotten that we belong to each other.” That is never truer than in the church. This new society that Jesus calls His  church  is where we find connection to God and a sense of belonging.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 12:11-13:13
description: The human body is "fearfully and wonderfully made" (Psalm 139:14), and so is the church—the body of Christ. The church is far more than a polished, organizational machine; it's an organism filled with people who have been filled with life. But we are not the body of Christ individually; we are the body of Christ together, composed of each unique combination of spiritual gifts found in each believer. In this message from 1 Corinthians 12 and 13, Skip Heitzig shares about the equality and necessity of each part of the body of Christ.
speaker: Skip

title: Easter Sunrise - On the Road to Emmaus
description:
The resurrection of Jesus Christ is one of the most attested-to
facts in history, and it is a fact that sets Christianity apart from every
other world religion. For those who knew Jesus while He walked this earth, the
road to discovering and believing that Jesus was resurrected started in
disheartening confusion, but it ended in decisive confirmation. In this Easter
message, Skip Heitzig shares five principles to help us relate to the risen
Christ from the conversation Jesus had with two of His disciples on the road to
Emmaus.
speaker: Skip

title: On the Road to Jerusalem
description: Today, on Good Friday, and on Easter Sunday, we consider events that occurred while  on the road . As Jesus approached the city of Jerusalem for His atoning death and glorious resurrection, He was met on the road by a crowd of worshiping supporters who laid their garments on that road as Jesus entered their city. This singular event, traditionally called the triumphal entry, displays four attributes of God’s personality reflected in Christ’s life and ministry.
speaker: Skip

title: Church: A Place for Healing
description: The world is a cruel place because the effects of sin are virtually everywhere. The consequence is that people become broken, addicted, hardened, depressed, and unstable. Everywhere people go, they experience the coldness of rejection. Social, educational, and political institutions don’t help, but rather make things worse. The church of Jesus Christ could be and should be a place of healing—not by excusing wrongdoing, but by lifting people to a place of forgiveness and help.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 12:10
description: Spiritual gifts are spiritual capacities given by God to accomplish a work He wants to do in a particular situation. As believers, our highest capacity isn't to just be a pool collecting the refreshing waters of salvation, but to be a portal where those waters can flow into the lives of others. In this teaching, Skip Heitzig continues in 1 Corinthians 12, highlighting the gifts of prophecy and tongues as channels of a deeper work of God in the lives of believers.
speaker: Skip

title: Church: A Place for Acceptance
description:
The church—the gathering of
people that Jesus Christ promises to establish, head, and protect—sometimes
does not reflect to the world what He wants it to reflect. As a result, many
people view church as a place of condemnation and rejection rather than a place
of love and acceptance. In this message, Nate Heitzig teaches from James 4
about how our love for others, not our condemnation, can lead them to
repentance.
speaker: guest:Nate Heitzig

title: 1 Corinthians 12:9-10
description: We all employ a certain measure of faith in everyday situations—that the car will start, the bank will cash a check, the light will turn on when you push the switch. The gift of faith is a Spirit-given ability to see something that God wants done and to sustain unwavering confidence that God will do it, regardless of the obstacles. In this teaching from 1 Corinthians 12, Skip Heitzig explores the spiritual gifts of faith, healing, and prophecy as proof that God is not limited by natural laws.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 12:8
description: The gifts of the Spirit are diverse—varied gifts provided to meet the needs of different ministries—but each gift is given to believers "through the same Spirit" (1 Corinthians 12:8). Spiritual gifts are the gateway, not the goal. God doesn't give a gift to fulfill the individual in the use of that gift, but for the edification of the body of Christ. In this teaching from 1 Corinthians 12, Skip Heitzig explains the differences between the gifts of the word of wisdom and the word of knowledge.
speaker: Skip

title: We Are God's House: 40 Years of Life Change
description: How does a church celebrate forty years of ministry? With huge smiles and grateful hearts! We are rejoicing in the scores of people whose lives have been changed, whose marriages have been healed, whose losses have been softened, whose ministries have been launched, and whose faith has been strengthened. This weekend we look back with gratitude and we look forward with confidence. Let’s consider what Peter tells us about this spiritual house we call our church family.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 12:1-8
description: It's one thing to have water in a reservoir—contained, always there if you need it. It's quite another to have water that pours out of you. So, not only do you have it when you need it, but there's so much of it that not only are you refreshed, but everyone around you gets splashed. That's the kind of life believers have through the Holy Spirit. In this message, Skip Heitzig teaches from 1 Corinthians 12, where the apostle Paul explained how spiritual gifts work in the context of Christian community.
speaker: Skip

title: Confronting the Prince of Darkness
description: As we have seen in this series, some of the Bible’s greatest heroes had darkroom experiences. They were developed by those painful experiences and used by God to impact their world. Today we examine Jesus Himself, the Light of the World (see John 8:12), facing off with the Prince of Darkness (see Ephesians 6:12). Five adjectives describe this confrontation, giving us insight into both the nature of temptation and the resolve of Jesus to follow His Father’s plan for saving the world.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 11
description: Our relationship with God should always be in the present tense. Too many Christians say, "I remember what it was like in the good ol' days." But are you walking with Him now? Is He speaking to you now? If your relationship with God is only a past-tense experience, it needs to be brought into the present. In this teaching, Skip Heitzig encourages you to continue in your walk with the Lord daily.
speaker: Skip

title: Facing Darkness with Grace
description: How do you face dark times? Notice I didn’t ask how  should  you face dark times, but rather how  do  you? Pain and suffering are universal, but for the Christian, they are valuable and even beneficial. Today we take a look at the apostle Paul’s own personal experience. He had a very positive episode followed by a very negative one. It rattled him at first, but eventually he learned a lesson that lifted him to a place where he could face the darkness with confidence and grace.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 10:11-11:1
description: As believers, we are free in Christ, and we have been set free from the law of Moses. But Christian liberty comes with Christian responsibility—responsibility to the Lord, to edify other believers, and to amplify the Word, work, and truth of God in our own lives. In this message from 1 Corinthians 10, Skip Heitzig shares how we can avoid abusing the liberty we have in Christ.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 10:1-13
description: When the children of Israel were delivered from Egypt, their journey through the desert was off to a great start. But a good start doesn't guarantee a great finish. Temptations always come, but the Lord will provide a way to escape—it's up to us to take it. In this teaching from 1 Corinthians 10, Skip Heitzig encourages us to continue in our daily walk with an attitude of deliverance and freedom, a reflection of the glorious liberty we have in Christ.
speaker: Skip

title: How to Live (and Love) in the Last Days
description: Welcome to one of our most cherished weekends of the year—Love Bomb weekend. We love it so much because we know that as a result, people will be changed by it. The fruit produced in the next forty-eight hours will impact some who have never heard of God’s love in Christ, but they will shortly. Today we consider the words of Peter to believers who were struggling under the weight of Roman tyranny and oppression. He encourages them to wait expectantly for Jesus to return, but in the meantime to live their lives with three elements in place so they can stay strong and vibrant.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 9
description: Throughout his ministry, the apostle Paul was driven by the calling God placed on his life. Where are you going? How's your race? We each have our own race, our own goal, our own calling, and our own decisions to make. In this message, Skip Heitzig shares how our calling and the love of God in Christ propel us through our daily lives.
speaker: Skip

title: When Society Grows Dark
description: Every culture ebbs and flows as it marches toward extinction. The great Roman Empire, the Mayan civilization, Bronze Age Greece—every complex society in history has eventually collapsed. Daniel was in the midst of the great Babylonian Empire (also extinct today). As a godly and faithful man, he experienced the darkness of an oppressive government. When the foundation of society crumbles, where do you go for solid footing and how should you respond?
speaker: Skip

title: The Darkness of a Broken Family
description: One of the darkest rooms anyone can enter is dealing with a broken family. To be part of a family that is fragmented and malfunctioning feels bleak and miserable. The by-products of being in such a family are feeling unwanted, unloved, and isolated. But did you know that many people in Scripture came from such families, including David? The good news is that God is in the business of fixing broken things, including broken families. David’s darkroom of family difficulty is what we consider here.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 7:25-8:13
description: When it comes to the gray areas of life, it can be simple to spot certain wrongs when viewed through the lens of Scripture. But it's also possible for those gray areas to create friction between believers. In this message from 1 Corinthians, Skip Heitzig reminds us why we must know and understand the difference between the essentials and the nonessentials of our faith.
speaker: Skip

title: Choosing to "Go Dark"
description: Though dark circumstances are everyone’s lot, no one deliberately chooses a gloomy experience. Why opt for pain when you can have pleasure? Why pick suffering when you can have solace? But Moses did exactly that. Moses was a man who made the deliberate choice to suffer. He picked the darkroom! Why he did that, how he did that, and what became of that choice are the basis for his story and his fame. We remember Moses because of his personal choice to “go dark.”
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 7:1-28
description: Relationships are the essence of life. Strip away all the things you own, all the degrees you've worked for, and all the beauty you strive to attain. When you get right down to the very basics of life, it's your relationship with God and your relationships with people that matter. In this teaching, Skip Heitzig shares from 1 Corinthians 7 about how healthy relationships glorify God on earth.
speaker: Skip

title: Welcome to the Darkroom
description: Just as photographs were once developed in a darkroom, so God develops our lives through dark and difficult times. A photographer works to make a beautiful picture come to life in the dim light of that environment, and God develops us in the gloomiest of circumstances. He’s done it for years and He’s done it with great success. God’s best workers have emerged from the darkest moments to make the greatest impact. Joseph was one of them. Pockmarked by early hardship in life, Joseph eventually got thrown into a dark dungeon. But that’s just the beginning of his story!
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 6
description: When God wants to do something on earth, He does it through His church. We are His hands and feet. We are His mouthpieces. But the body can sometimes get infected. The church at Corinth was infected with issues that still affect the church today, including disputes within the church. In this message, Skip Heitzig highlights the importance of following biblical guidelines to settle disputes between believers.
speaker: Skip

title: A Sermon on Six Legs
description: Most people think of ants as a nuisance to be eliminated, but Solomon saw them as teachers to be emulated. Writing to his son (see Proverbs 6:1), Solomon warns him that though rest is good, too much of it can be bad. As we conclude our Hustle and Grind series, we focus on the comparison between the industrious ant and the inactive sluggard and why work and rest must be kept in careful balance.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 5
description: Jesus knew that His followers would be surrounded by people who have a different value system and He asked His Father to "keep [us] from the evil one" (John 17:15). But He never intended that we remove ourselves from the world. In this teaching, Pastor Skip reminds us that we are not called to be isolated from the world, but we have been set free and called to live pure lives as an example in and to the world.
speaker: Skip

title: A Thrill of Hope
description: So many of the great songs of the Christmas season have hope as the theme. Perhaps the most famous is the familiar hymn from 1847 “O Holy Night,” which describes the thrill of hope as the weary world rejoices. There are two people in the Christmas story who are usually overlooked, but who embodied this hope as they waited with expectation for years on end for Jesus’ birth. They are Simeon and Anna, and these two are great examples of what it means biblically to have hope.
speaker: Skip

title: How Joseph Gave Us Christmas
description: In the Christmas story, Jesus understandably gets top billing. Mary follows as a close second, again rightfully so since she was a young virgin girl who miraculously turned up pregnant with Israel’s Messiah. But then there’s Joseph. Though he is part of the nativity scene, he is regarded as almost incidental or supplemental, like a bystander. Today, we will follow Joseph’s uneasy emotional journey from Nazareth to the manger as we consider his role and reaction to it.
speaker: Skip

title: The Sabbath Rest
description: Though Christians are solidly under the new covenant, rooted in grace and not law, we enjoy the principle of taking a  Sabbath rest  from our work. We bring honor to God by worshipful rest. We also show respect to others in our lives by using our free time to build them up. Not only that but we need a break for our physical health and emotional health. Today, let’s consider not only God’s commandment for us to rest, but also the stewardship of our time in putting it into practice.
speaker: Skip

title: Learning to Relax
description: If ever there was a commandment tailor-made for the overcommitted and overworked, this is it! Here, God gives His people an order to rest and relax. It’s pretty amazing that we serve a God who put this on His top ten list of important things. Today and next week we will consider what it means to rest and why it is good to do so. Moreover, we’ll see why it is essential to our worship.
speaker: Skip

title: When Work Becomes an Idol
description: America is founded on hard work; we even dedicate a day (Labor Day) to celebrate workers. The American Dream suggests that wealth and success follow hard work, and Scripture commends work that’s well done (see Colossians 3:23-24). But something good can become bad if taken too far. Work is good; overwork is not. Being a worker is good, while being a workaholic is bad. Work can become an idol, interrupting the priority of God in our life. Psalm 127 is a poem of contrasting priorities—a life of vanity versus a life of value—and in it we find several warnings from its author, Solomon.
speaker: Skip

title: What Does It Mean to Be a Disciple?
description: The word  disciple  is common in Christian circles, and though the meanings of words change over time, we have the  job description  straight from Jesus’ mouth. Many of us willingly call ourselves disciples, but have we really delved into what Jesus meant by it? When He invited those in His circle to follow Him, He outlined what it would take. He wanted them to count the cost. And He wanted them to know the reward.
speaker: Skip

title: Get to Work!
description: For American adults, over 70 percent of time awake is spent in the workplace. That means the workplace is the greatest mission field of our day. But for some, a wall exists between Sunday and Monday separating their spiritual life from their work life. In this message, Nate Heitzig teaches from Nehemiah 2-3 and gleans biblical principles on how to work with purpose, people, and passion.
speaker: guest:Nate Heitzig

title: 1 Corinthians 2:14-4:21
description: In the second chapter of 1 Corinthians, Paul explained that the foundation of the church is Christ and the growth of each believer is dependent on the Word of God, not on the teachings of individuals. In this teaching, Pastor Skip reminds us that no foundation for the church can be laid beyond what God already laid in His Son, Jesus Christ.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Corinthians 1:17-2:16
description: In this letter, the apostle Paul addressed the problems faced by a growing fellowship of new believers, problems every church faces because the church is filled with sinners—those humbled and broken people who are God's chosen people. In this teaching, Pastor Skip reminds us that God so often uses the small, broken things to share His love with the world.
speaker: Skip

title: A Courage Revival
description: Johnnie Moore is an author, businessperson, and itinerant pastor who is best known for his religious freedom advocacy all around the world. His latest book,  The Next Jihad , is about the persecution of Christians in Africa. He is the recipient of many awards and honors, including the prestigious Medal of Valor from the Simon Wiesenthal Center in Los Angeles. He has been twice appointed to the US Commission for International Religious Freedom by the president of the United States.
speaker: guest:Johnnie Moore

title: 1 Corinthians 1:1-20
description: In this first teaching in the book of 1 Corinthians, Skip Heitzig introduces the city of Corinth, a financial and economic center of the ancient world. Against the backdrop of a city mired in immorality, the apostle Paul called on believers to be set apart from the world as saints whose primary identity is rooted in Christ.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 30-31
description: In 1 Samuel 30-31, David strengthened himself in the Lord and recovered what had been lost, while Saul’s life ended in defeat and dishonor. Two endings—one king restored, one king ruined. When we seek God in our brokenness, He brings victory; but rejecting Him always leads to ruin.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Religion
description: Religion might not seem like a giant to overcome unless you’re an atheist. But did you know the source of much persecution and oppression around the world is religious groups? The prophets, the apostles, the early church, and even Jesus Himself all had run-ins with religious leaders and formalized religious systems. Some of you come from a very religious background but now enjoy the freedom of a relationship with God through Jesus. How does one successfully stand up to religious pressure while impacting it with the gospel? Let’s see how Stephen did it.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 28-29
description: As Saul turned to a medium for guidance, David was dismissed from battle by the Philistines—two kings moving in opposite directions. We step into danger when we drift from God’s voice, but even then, there is grace in divine redirection, whether we choose to recognize it or not.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Overwhelming Odds
description: By now you have discovered that we who are Christians are surrounded! There seems to always be more who are against us than who are for us. We face the reality (and we feel it, too!) that we are living in enemy territory. That doesn’t give us permission to be adversarial or combative, for we’ll attract more flies with honey than with vinegar (see 2 Timothy 2:24-25). But Christians are either overcome by their unbelief or they are overcomers because of their faith. How do we navigate through life when the odds are stacked against us and circumstances seem overwhelming?
speaker: Skip

title: Skip Heitzig Interviews Cissie Graham Lynch, Vince Torres, and Lenya Heitzig
description: In this special service, Skip Heitzig interviews Cissie Graham Lynch, Vince Torres, and Lenya Heitzig. Cissie Graham Lynch is the host of the podcast Fearless, in which she discusses living with a fearless faith in a compromising culture. Vince Torres is president of the Family Policy Alliance of New Mexico, and he joins us to discuss political issues facing Christian families today. Finally is Reload Love founder Lenya Heitzig, who speaks about the global efforts to fight terrorism and how everyday people can help.
speaker: Skip

title: Addressing Deconstruction and Cancel Culture
description: Sean McDowell is a sought-after international speaker on cultural, ethical, theological, and apologetics topics, and he retains a PhD in Apologetics and Worldview Studies from Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. He has authored and co-authored over one dozen books and study guides, including  So the Next Generation Will Know: Preparing Young Christians for a Challenging World  and  Chasing Love.
speaker: guest:Sean McDowell

title: 1 Samuel 26-27
description: Moments of boldness can still be followed by lapses in trust—but God works even in the wandering. In 1 Samuel 26-27, David again spared Saul’s life, proving his loyalty, but took refuge in enemy territory out of fear. He was faithful yet flawed but God's provisions were never diminished by David's missteps.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Self: How One Person Can Make a Difference
description: On this weekend that commemorates the tragedy of September 11, 2001, we especially honor those who gave their lives in trying to rescue others, especially the first responders in law enforcement and fire departments, as well as citizens. Journalist Geraldine Brooks reminds us, “September 11, 2001, revealed heroism in ordinary people who might have gone through their lives never called upon to demonstrate the extent of their courage.” Today we look at the story of Esther’s choice to put  self  aside and make a difference for those facing death. Here we see the extent of her courage!
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 24-25
description: True strength is seen not in retaliation but in restraint—and the confidence that God's justice is always better than ours. David learned to let God be his defender when he spared Saul's life in a cave and was later restrained from vengeance through Abigail's wisdom.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Fear
description: One of the most paralyzing of all human emotions is fear. It can rob us of reason and faith. It makes a bad situation worse than it really is, and it saps us of energy and confidence. David would write later on, “I sought the  Lord , and He heard me, and delivered me from all my fears” (Psalm 34:4). But in our story today he faced a fearsome giant (literally) that his country was in dread of. Let’s consider how fear works and by what means it can be defeated.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 22-23
description: Godly leaders seek God’s direction and value people over position. David became a leader of outcasts while Saul continued his spiral into rage and destruction. In contrast to Saul’s cruelty and refusal to accept responsibility for his wrongdoings, David sought the Lord's guidance and chose to follow His command, despite his own fear and uncertainty.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Apathy
description: The Oxford Dictionary defines  apathy  as “lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.” It’s the state of being indifferent to something that should otherwise arouse, provoke, or motivate you. It has been noted that cooling down a fanatic is easier than warming up a corpse. When a person ceases to care, that person ceases to attempt change. Though Nehemiah had it made in terms of his earthly status, the condition in his homeland wouldn’t let him stay silent and inactive. Let’s explore the five steps he took to overcome the giant of apathy.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 21-22:2
description: Panic often leads to compromise. On the run and desperate, David sought help from priests and strangers, but fear drove his decisions. Though God provided, David’s fear led to devastating consequences. We must remember that God remains faithful even when face uncertainty.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Silence
description: "Silence is golden," says the old adage. But that is true only sometimes. Many other times, to be silent is to be complicit in the evil that is being committed around us. John the Baptist, one of the most outspoken prophetic voices in history, helps us navigate the need to speak out against evil and immorality. He confronted a powerful political leader of his day, pointing out where he had violated God’s law. John was imprisoned and executed as a result. Should Christians enter the public square to dialogue about moral issues? Yes, but let’s see how.
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 19-20
description: Godly friendships reflect covenant faithfulness and often shine brightest in times of hardship. Because Saul’s jealousy grew, David’s life was in danger—but his friendship with Jonathan became a lifeline. Through loyalty and love, Jonathan risked everything to protect him.
speaker: Skip

title: The Giant of Conformity
description: There are giants in the land, both moral and spiritual, and we need courage to confront them! Truth is, the world around us is not at all sympathetic to the Christian cause. In fact, they would like nothing more than to silence us and make us conform to their standards. As our Lord said, “The world would love you as one of its own if you belonged to it, but you are no longer part of the world. I chose you to come out of the world, so it hates you” (John 15:19, NLT). Daniel and his three friends were pressured to conform, but they refused. Let’s find out the source of their strength to make such a courageous stand.
speaker: Skip

title: The Chosen
description: An estimated 194 million people have already seen the popular series  The Chosen , based on the life and ministry of Jesus Christ. The goal, according to producer Dallas Jenkins, is to reach one billion people, and they are well on their way to reaching that goal. As we close out our Now Streaming series, let’s dig into Jesus’ own announcement to His disciples that they were chosen by Him. What does it mean to be chosen by God? What are we chosen for? What plans does He have for us once we’ve been chosen?
speaker: Skip

title: 1 Samuel 17:28-18:30
description: Though we wish we could escape the painful experiences of life, they are purposeful. David's early years were peaceful, but His life changed forever when a prophet anointed him for God's special purpose. In this study, we witness the legendary showdown between David and Goliath, as well as David's growing renown and King Saul's growing insecurity. Discover how David's own life pointed to a future King and how your faith can grow in difficult circumstances.
speaker: Skip

title: The Modern (Church) Family
description: Jesus stated His intention to build His church (see Matthew 16:18). What He had in mind was a family of sorts—a new community made up of people as diverse as there are people in the world (see Acts 2:44). Many of us would not naturally hang out together. Our differences may be profound, our viewpoints and backgrounds may be in conflict, and our ideas may seem incompatible. But there is a glue that is stronger than all that. We are  in Christ . And if Jesus is your Savior and God is your Father, that makes us a modern family.
speaker: Skip

title: The Last Dance: Instructions on How to Die Well
description: Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote,  “A grave, wherever found, preaches a short and pithy sermon to the soul.”  What did he mean?
